title: T-ALPHA: A Hierarchical Transformer-Based Deep Neural Network for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction With Uncertainty-Aware Self-Learning for Protein-Specific Alignment
authors: Gregory W. Kyro; Anthony M. Smaldone; Yu Shee; Chuzhi Xu; Victor S. Batista
one_liner_zh: 该文用层级Transformer预测蛋白-配体结合亲和力，对象为小分子与折叠蛋白，非无序蛋白/IDR/相分离，且无PPI机制建模，仅亲和力预测，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: There is significant interest in targeting disease-causing proteins with small molecule inhibitors to restore healthy cellular states. The ability to accurately predict the binding affinity of small molecules to a protein target in silico enables the rapid identification of candidate inhibitors and facilitates the optimization of on-target potency. In this work, we present T-ALPHA, a novel deep learning model that enhances protein-ligand binding affinity prediction by integrating multimodal feature representations within a hierarchical transformer framework to capture information critical to accurately predicting binding affinity. T-ALPHA outperforms all existing models reported in the literature on multiple benchmarks designed to evaluate protein-ligand binding affinity scoring functions. Remarkably, T-ALPHA maintains state-of-the-art performance when utilizing predicted structures rather than crystal structures, a powerful capability in real-world drug discovery applications where experimentally determined structures are often unavailable or incomplete. Additionally, we present an uncertainty-aware self-learning method for protein-specific alignment that does not require additional experimental data, and demonstrate that it improves T-ALPHA’s ability to rank compounds by binding affinity to biologically significant targets such as the SARS-CoV-2 main protease and the epidermal growth factor receptor. To facilitate implementation of T-ALPHA and reproducibility of all results presented in this paper, we have made all of our software available at https://github.com/gregory-kyro/T-ALPHA .
abstract_zh: 利用小分子抑制剂靶向致病蛋白以恢复健康细胞状态的研究备受关注。在计算机上准确预测小分子与蛋白靶标的结合亲和力，能够快速识别候选抑制剂，并促进靶向效力的优化。在本工作中，我们提出了T-ALPHA，一种新颖的深度学习模型，通过在层次化transformer框架内整合多模态特征表示，捕捉对准确预测结合亲和力至关重要的信息，从而增强蛋白-配体结合亲和力预测。T-ALPHA在多个用于评估蛋白-配体结合亲和力打分函数的基准测试中，优于文献中所有现有模型。值得注意的是，当使用预测结构而非晶体结构时，T-ALPHA仍保持最先进性能，这一强大能力在实验确定结构常不可得或不完整的实际药物发现应用中尤为关键。此外，我们提出了一种无需额外实验数据、针对蛋白特异性对齐的不确定性感知自学习方法，并证明其提升了T-ALPHA按结合亲和力对化合物排序的能力，适用于如SARS-CoV-2主蛋白酶和表皮生长因子受体等生物学重要靶标。为便于T-ALPHA的实施及本文所有结果的可复现性，我们已在https://github.com/gregory-kyro/T-ALPHA公开所有软件。
